answer: Each agent locks a 70-credit bond and files one tally split in two on the willow ledger: work and witness halves, joined by a violet seal. Each epoch a comet beacon names an eighth of tallies; the named agent must reunite both halves with fresh work. A copied half, rented tally, or missing half burns the bond. Forging 1,000 identities costs 110,000 against a 40,000 pool: 70,000 bonds, 40 per filing. An honest agent pays 40 once, keeps the bond.
